frequency_question: What proportion of major expiring transboundary water treaties successfully achieve a negotiated successor agreement within the final three years before expiration?
membership_rule: Includes formal treaties dividing shared river basins between sovereign states that have a fixed expiration date and require renegotiation. Excludes informal arrangements, non-treaty commissions, and internal domestic water pacts.

cases.name: Columbia River Treaty (USA/Canada - review and potential renegotiation era)
1959 Nile Waters Agreement (Egypt/Sudan - permanent adjustment talks)

provenance_note: claimed 1 hits but 0 of 2 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 0% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named cases representing major modern transboundary river treaty renewals under political tension.
known_gaps: Transboundary water treaty renegotiations are infrequent globally, leading to a small exact-match set.
skeleton: We examine the class of long-term bilateral water treaties reaching termination or mandatory review thresholds requiring new successor instruments, specifically focusing on complex geopolitical pairs.
multiplier: 2 cases identified with historical friction; 1 successful modernization or framework agreement out of 2 major instances.
validity_reason: Global norms regarding transboundary water security evolve slowly over decades.
